questions.topic: Graph Representations: Adjacency Lists in Practice
questions.question: What does an adjacency list store for each graph vertex?
options: Only that vertex's outgoing neighbors
One cell for every possible vertex pair
The complete traversal history from every entry point
Every query vector ever compared with the vertex

questions.topic: Graph Representations: Adjacency Lists in Practice
questions.question: What is the space complexity of adjacency lists?
options: O(V squared)
O(V + E)
O(log V)
O(E squared)

questions.topic: Graph Representations: Adjacency Lists in Practice
questions.question: Why is an adjacency matrix wasteful for one million vertices with 32 neighbors each?
options: It cannot answer whether a particular edge exists
It stores each present edge without any absent-edge cells
It reserves space for nearly a trillion mostly absent vertex pairs
It always uses less than one bit for each possible directed edge

questions.topic: Graph Representations: Adjacency Lists in Practice
questions.question: How does a compressed sparse row-style graph represent neighbor lists?
options: As one heap object and hash table for each stored edge
As a dense V-by-V matrix plus one list of missing edges
As one linked node allocated remotely for every neighbor ID
As an offsets array indexing ranges in one flat neighbors array

questions.topic: Graph Representations: Adjacency Lists in Practice
questions.question: Why might a directed nearest-neighbor graph lack the reverse edge B to A?
options: A can rank B among its nearest neighbors without B ranking A among its own
Directed graphs require every connection to be stored symmetrically
Nearest-neighbor relations are always transitive but never asymmetric
Reverse edges are represented automatically by the vertex offset array

questions.topic: Graph Representations: Adjacency Lists in Practice
questions.question: What is the central degree tradeoff in a retrieval graph?
options: Lower degree always improves connectivity and increases search branching
More edges improve routes but increase memory and work per expansion
Degree changes vector dimension but not graph storage or traversal
Higher degree guarantees exact nearest neighbors with one visited vertex

questions.question: What move does pure greedy nearest-neighbor traversal make?
options: Move to a random unvisited vertex anywhere in the graph
Move to the neighbor farthest from both entry and query
Move to the closest neighbor only when it improves query distance
Move through every neighbor before computing any query distance

questions.question: Why should traversal maintain a visited set?
options: To force every vertex in the corpus to be evaluated
To convert directed edges into undirected edges permanently
To sort all vectors by document ID before computing distance
To prevent cycles from causing repeated expansion

questions.question: The query is (9,9), and candidates B=(4,3) and C=(2,5) are adjacent to the entry. Which is greedily preferred by Euclidean distance?
options: B, because its distance is about 7.81 versus C's 8.06
C, because its first coordinate is smaller than B's
Both, because all two-dimensional points have equal query distance
Neither, because greedy traversal cannot compare two neighbors

questions.question: If traversal visits v vertices of degree M using d-dimensional vectors, what rough distance-computation cost applies?
options: O(v + M + d)
O(vMd)
O(log(vMd))
O(d raised to vM)

questions.question: How does best-first traversal improve recall over a single greedy path?
options: It removes all distance calculations after the entry point
It guarantees exact search without regard to connectivity
It preserves and expands alternative promising candidates after one path stalls
It replaces the graph with a complete adjacency matrix for each query

questions.question: Why can multiple entry points improve graph search?
options: They ensure every entry belongs to the same disconnected component
They reduce vector dimensionality before any comparison
They make visit budgets and tie-breaking unnecessary
They reduce dependence on one start landing in the correct basin

questions.topic: Local Minima in Greedy Search and Why Layered Graphs Help
questions.question: What is a local minimum in greedy graph search?
options: A vertex closer than all stored neighbors but not globally closest
The globally closest vertex with an edge to every other vertex
A vertex whose vector has the smallest numerical coordinate
An entry point selected from the sparsest graph layer

questions.topic: Local Minima in Greedy Search and Why Layered Graphs Help
questions.question: Why can pure greedy traversal fail to escape a local minimum?
options: It always explores every temporarily worse neighbor before stopping
Reaching a better region may first require a move that worsens distance
It maintains too many alternative candidates in a priority queue
A local minimum always belongs to the true nearest-neighbor component

questions.topic: Local Minima in Greedy Search and Why Layered Graphs Help
questions.question: What role does a sparse upper graph play in layered search?
options: It stores every local edge and performs final exact refinement
It removes long-range links so search remains inside the entry cluster
It supplies long-range navigation before descent to denser local layers
It replaces query distance with insertion order as the routing signal

questions.topic: Local Minima in Greedy Search and Why Layered Graphs Help
questions.question: What is the extreme failure represented by disconnected components?
options: The true region requires one temporarily worse step
The candidate queue contains too many equal-score vertices
Upper-layer links cross the corpus in too few hops
No edge path from the entry can reach the true region

questions.topic: Local Minima in Greedy Search and Why Layered Graphs Help
questions.question: Why do layers combine long-range and local links?
options: Different scales support global routing and fine destination refinement
Every scale needs identical edges to guarantee one-hop exact search
Local links are best for crossing the corpus while long links refine neighbors
Layering eliminates all memory and construction tradeoffs

questions.topic: Local Minima in Greedy Search and Why Layered Graphs Help
questions.question: A recall miss occurred because the true component was unreachable. Which remedy targets the diagnosed mechanism?
options: Decrease every vector's numerical precision without rebuilding edges
Improve graph construction and connectivity between regions
Shorten the visit budget so traversal stops even earlier
Change deterministic tie-breaking while preserving disconnected components
